explanations: terra: Remembering God's favor is followed by “fulfil My covenant and I will fulfil yours,” an explicit divine-gift and human-response relation rather than a merely verbal root match.
terra: God's command to slaughter a cow is a specific divinely ordered animal-killing scene, though the animal is not described as an offering or sanctuary-bound.
terra: The people finally slaughter the cow, completing the commanded act; its relevance remains limited because the narrative purpose is not sacrificial worship.
terra: God makes the House a place of return and security and commands its purification for worshippers, identifying the sanctuary as an appointed destination prepared for rites.
terra: Beside the House, Abraham and Ishmael ask God to show them their مَنَاسِك; the sanctuary offering belongs to rites received through divine instruction.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to turn his face toward the Sacred Mosque; human orientation toward the sanctuary forms a nonlexical parallel to the hedy's directed journey.
terra: The command to face the Sacred Mosque is repeated as truth from the Lord, supplying the directed sanctuary movement whose favor-and-guidance purpose 2:150 then states.

terra: The command to turn toward the Sacred Mosque culminates in God's completing His favor and in the people being guided; sanctuary-directed orientation, نِعْمَتِي, and تَهْتَدُونَ meet in one ayah.
terra: Safa and Marwa are God's ritual signs, and voluntary good is met by God's appreciation; the sanctuary rite is presented as a freely offered response that God acknowledges.
terra: Believers are told to eat the good things God provided and thank Him; it gives the same provision-to-gratitude sequence without using the section's animal vocabulary.
terra: The prohibition of carrion, blood, pork, and what is dedicated to another establishes a repeated food-and-slaughter boundary around an offering directed to God.
terra: Completing the fast leads to magnifying God عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَاكُمْ and to gratitude; it repeats the guidance-to-glorification formula attached to sacrificed livestock in 22:37.

luna: The section's dictionary form الهدي is an animal led to the Haram; this ayah says the هَدْي reaches its مَحِلّ, the destination that makes the animal's directed movement concrete. | terra: حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّهُ names the hedy and its appointed destination, directly staging the sanctuary-bound animal contained in the section's ه د ي wordplay.
terra: After completing the rites, pilgrims are commanded to remember God intensely; ritual completion is answered by speech, as the section distinguishes its surah's verbal response.
terra: Believers must give from good things they earned and received from the earth rather than choose defective goods, adding a quality boundary to what is returned.
terra: Good expenditure is directed toward seeking God's face and returns in full to the giver, articulating the intention behind a nontransactional counter-gift.
terra: Attaining righteousness requires spending from what one loves; it explains why returning a valuable animal can signify more than transferring flesh.
terra: The House at Bakkah is blessed and هُدًى لِلْعَالَمِينَ; the destination of the hedy is itself described as guidance, sharpening the root's two directions.
terra: The House contains clear signs and security, and pilgrimage to it is owed to God by those able to make the way; the sanctuary destination is itself a human offering of duty.
terra: A demanded قُرْبَان تَأْكُلُهُ النَّار is made a condition for trusting a messenger; the reply exposes sacrifice used as an evidentiary demand rather than grateful obedience.
terra: Livestock are made lawful while hunting is barred in consecration; the ayah marks the sacred-state legal boundary within which sanctuary offerings operate.

luna: The section's dictionary form الهدي names animals sent toward the Haram. This ayah protects الْهَدْي among the sacred rites and describes people approaching the Sacred House seeking bounty and approval from their Lord. | terra: The ayah protects الْهَدْيَ and its garlands while also naming people heading for the Sacred House, placing offering and sanctuary-directed movement in one scene.
terra: Animals dedicated to other than God or slaughtered on altars are forbidden, while the same ayah speaks of God's completed نِعْمَة; divine favor does not license a misdirected counter-offering.
terra: God says ritual purification is meant to complete His favor so that people may give thanks, another explicit favor-to-gratitude sequence.
terra: Each son of Adam offers a قُرْبَان, but acceptance belongs to the God-fearing; this supplies the acceptance-and-taqwa dimension later made explicit for sacrificial flesh in 22:37.
terra: Accessible game tests whether consecrated pilgrims fear God unseen; it explains the violated boundary for which 5:95 requires a hedy reaching the Kaaba.

luna: This ayah specifies a livestock offering هَدْيًا بَالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ, an animal that must reach the Kaaba. It gives a concrete instance of the section's Harem-bound hedy. | terra: هَدْيًا بَالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ makes an equivalent livestock offering travel to the Kaaba as expiation, stating both the animal and the destination.

luna: The section centers on an animal presented at the Haram. In the adjacent pilgrimage rule, this ayah permits sea game but bars land game during ihram, completing 5:95's contrast between hunted game and livestock sent as an offering. | terra: Land game is forbidden while pilgrims are consecrated, supplying the ritual animal boundary within which 5:95 prescribes a livestock offering to the Kaaba.

luna: This ayah groups الْهَدْيَ with the Sacred House, sacred month, and garlands as things made to uphold people's religious life; it shows the sent animal functioning as a sacred sign. | terra: The Kaaba, sacred month, hedy, and garlands are made supports for people; it locates the consecrated animal inside the ordered sanctuary system.
terra: God did not institute the bahira, sa'iba, wasila, or ham; these invented consecrations mark the boundary between prescribed hedy and livestock made sacred by human fabrication.
terra: Eating what God's name has been mentioned over makes utterance part of lawful animal food, matching the spoken naming over sacrificial livestock.
terra: The ayah asks why believers should not eat what God's name has been mentioned over, continuing 6:118's positive side of spoken naming and anticipating 6:121's prohibition.
terra: The command not to eat what God's name was not mentioned over supplies the negative boundary to the spoken naming that accompanies sacrificial livestock in 22:28, 22:34, and 22:36.
terra: People allot shares of crops and livestock created by God to Him and to their partners; it is the section's returned-gift motion corrupted by a false recipient and false accounting.
terra: Invented rules forbid certain livestock and suppress God's name over others; this reverses the authorized offering over which His name is spoken.
terra: Livestock for load and for food are followed by كُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ; the ن ع م animal is first divine provision before it can become an offering.

luna: The section's secondary dictionary sense says hady can mean camels; this ayah names camels among livestock pairs. That anchors the animal sense only: the ayah itself debates animal restrictions and does not describe a Hady offering.
terra: Among the forbidden foods is a sinful animal dedicated to other than God, making the spoken recipient decisive for the animal's status.

luna: The section reads sacrifice as something presented to the Lord in response to His gift. This ayah explicitly places وَنُسُكِي, “my sacrifice/rite,” alongside prayer and says they are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. | terra: The commanded declaration إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي ... لِلَّهِ dedicates prayer and sacrifice to God, closely matching 108:2 while making the offering itself a spoken avowal.
terra: The declaration that God has no partner completes 6:162's dedication of prayer and sacrifice, excluding every rival recipient from the offering.
terra: Salih identifies God's she-camel as a sign, grants it pasture, and forbids harm; a divinely marked animal here must be protected rather than offered for slaughter.
terra: The people hamstring the protected she-camel and defy their messenger, turning animal killing into disobedience rather than worship.

luna: The section's dictionary note ties the ḍuḥā root to the Eid offering; here the same forenoon word marks a time when divine punishment may reach a town at play. This is only a contrast in the time's valence, since the ayah itself describes no sacrifice.
terra: God tells Moses to take what He has given him and be among the grateful, a concise formulation of reception followed by response.
terra: Those who are pleased only إِنْ أُعْطُوا from the alms and angry when not given reverse the proper response to gift: satisfaction becomes acquisitive and conditional.
terra: Some believers take what they spend as قُرُبَاتٍ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ; expenditure becomes a means of nearness, the broader devotional motion named by an offering.
terra: Salih again names God's she-camel as a sign, orders that it graze, and warns against harming it, repeating the protected-animal boundary.
terra: After the people hamstring the she-camel, they receive a three-day deadline; the killing's consequence confirms that consecration alone does not authorize sacrifice.
terra: The messengers bring Abraham glad tidings and he promptly brings them a roasted calf; received good news and an animal offered in hospitality occupy the same ayah.
terra: When the guests' hands do not reach the calf Abraham grows apprehensive; the offered animal's failure to reach its recipients contrasts with hedy reaching its appointed place.
terra: Abraham's wife receives the announcement of Isaac and then Jacob, completing the divine gift of offspring beside the preceding calf-offering scene.
terra: Paradise is called an uncut عَطَاء; this may illuminate the named noun by contrasting an enduring divine gift with a consumable offering, but the bridge is indirect.
terra: God's proclamation that gratitude brings increase makes explicit the responsive relation between a received favor and what the recipient does next.
terra: Abraham's prayer joins the Sacred House, established prayer, granted fruits, and لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ; sanctuary, provision, worship, and thanks form the section's larger pattern.

luna: The section's dictionary root ن ع م names livestock as well as blessing. This ayah says God created الْأَنْعَامَ for warmth, benefits, and food, making the animal itself a provision received from God. | terra: God creates الْأَنْعَامَ لَكُمْ with warmth, benefits, and food, making the animal side of ن ع م an expressly received good.
terra: The livestock's beauty appears when people drive them home and out to pasture; this ordinary directed herd movement supplies a concrete foil for the hedy driven to the sanctuary.
terra: Livestock carry human loads to a distant land; here the animal bears people toward a destination, complementing the section's animal that is itself conducted to one.
terra: Every favor people possess is said to be from God, fixing the original giver before the section considers any human return.
terra: The livestock contain drink given to people as pure milk; it makes provision emerge from the very animals whose root also names favor.
terra: God completes His favor so that people may submit, making surrender another response to completed gift.
terra: They recognize نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ and then deny it, the direct opposite of voicing and thanking the Lord's favor.
terra: A secure, well-provided town responds by denying God's favors and is made to taste hunger and fear, reversing both gratitude and the provision-security gifts of 106:4.
terra: People are told to eat God's lawful provision and وَاشْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ; received food calls for gratitude, as the offered animal is both provision and response.
terra: This repeated prohibition again excludes what is dedicated to another, reinforcing that animal slaughter is not a valid counter-offering merely because an animal is killed.

luna: The section pairs niʿma as blessing with h-d-y as guidance. This ayah portrays Abraham as grateful for God's favors and then guided to a straight path, bringing those two roots together in one account of divine favor and human response. | terra: Abraham is شَاكِرًا لِأَنْعُمِهِ and God هَدَاهُ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ; favor, grateful response, and guidance are explicitly joined.
terra: عَطَاءُ رَبِّكَ names the Lord's عطا as the thing extended to recipients, an exact Quranic use of the dictionary noun cited by the section.

luna: The section develops a meeting between the gift root ع ط و and the guidance root ه د ي. Moses' reply joins them in أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ, presenting giving and guidance as successive acts. | terra: رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ places giving and guiding together, the two named roots that form the received gift and directed movement in the section.

luna: The section's dictionary form الأضحية links ضحى to the Eid sacrifice. This ayah sets a gathering on the day of adornment at ضُحًى, a festival-day morning that makes the section's time association concrete. | terra: Moses fixes the encounter for يَوْمُ الزِّينَةِ and the people's gathering ضُحًى; without equating the festivals, the same daylight word appears in an expressly festive setting.
terra: God appoints Abraham the site of the House, excludes association, and commands its purification for pilgrims, preparing the place to which the animal rite later moves.

luna: The section's animal is driven toward a sacred destination. This ayah depicts pilgrims arriving for Hajj on lean camels from distant passes; 22:28 continues with the livestock offering and feeding, completing the arrival scene. | terra: Pilgrims come from every distant pass عَلَىٰ كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ; because the source section notes that hedy can name camels generally, this is the complementary camel journey toward the sanctuary.

luna: The section frames the animal as a God-given blessing that prompts a response. In the Hajj scene here, people mention God over the livestock He provided, then eat from it and feed the poor. | terra: Pilgrims name God over the livestock He provided, then eat and feed the destitute; provision, utterance, sacrifice, and sharing meet in one ayah.

luna: The section places the animal's arrival at the Haram within a pilgrimage. This ayah continues the rite by naming vows and circumambulation of the Ancient House; its own contribution is the human completion of the sanctuary visit. | terra: Pilgrims complete their rites, fulfil vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House; it carries the sacrificial sequence through to ritual completion at its sanctuary destination.

luna: This ayah joins honoring Allah's sacred ordinances to livestock made lawful under stated limits. It gives the section's sacred animal a frame of sanctuary law before the surrounding passage describes the rites and sacrificial animals. | terra: Honouring God's sacred ordinances is paired with the lawfulness of livestock and avoidance of idols, defining both the permitted animal and the false recipient excluded from sacrifice.
terra: Pure devotion without associating partners follows the command to avoid idols, clarifying the exclusive orientation of the nearby sacrificial rites.

luna: This ayah says honoring God's شعائر comes from taqwa of hearts; 22:33 next specifies the sacrificial animals and their place at the Ancient House. It frames the offering as a sacred sign whose outward honor rests on inward reverence. | terra: Honouring God's ritual signs is traced to the taqwa of hearts; 22:36 identifies the sacrificial camels as just such signs, preparing 22:37's account of what reaches God.

luna: The section's hedy is an animal moving toward a destination; this ayah describes benefits from sacrificial animals until an appointed time, then their place at the Ancient House. | terra: The ritual animals have benefits until an appointed term and then their destination is the Ancient House; the received benefit ends in an offered arrival.

luna: The section's source dictionary root ن ع م names camels as well as blessing. This ayah uses بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعَامِ for livestock over which God's name is mentioned, making the animal branch of that root part of a rite. | terra: Each community receives a rite so that God's name is mentioned over the livestock He provided; divine provision becomes an animal rite accompanied by spoken remembrance.

terra: The humble respond to God's mention with trembling, patience, prayer, and spending from His provision; this describes the inward and practical response immediately before the sacrificial camels.

luna: The section links the divine gift to a sacrificial return. This ayah names the sacrificial camels الْبُدْنَ, says there is good in them, directs people to feed the needy, and ends with gratitude. | terra: The sacrificial camels are God's signs and a خير for people; naming God over them, eating, feeding two kinds of poor, and giving thanks gather nearly every part of the section's animal-as-returned-gift image.

luna: This ayah bounds the section's reciprocal-sacrifice reading: the animals' flesh and blood do not reach God; taqwa does. The material offering matters as a rite, while the verse names what reaches God. | terra: Their flesh and blood do not reach God but taqwa does, while people magnify Him عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَاكُمْ; the ayah joins sacrifice to guidance and defines what truly reaches the giver.
terra: Every community is assigned a مَنْسَك, and the Prophet is said to stand عَلَىٰ هُدًى مُسْتَقِيمٍ; rite and guidance meet through the same pairing that drives the section.

luna: The section's source root ن ع م includes the animal sense; this ayah calls الْأَنْعَامِ a lesson and names drink, benefits, and food received from them, presenting livestock as a divine provision. | terra: The livestock provide drink, many benefits, and food; the repeated formulation reinforces that a sacrificial animal is also a bundle of gifts relinquished.
terra: Moses challenges Pharaoh's claimed “favor” by pointing to Israel's enslavement; it exposes favor-language used to demand gratitude for an injustice.
terra: God's aid is specified as livestock and sons, directly presenting الْأَنْعَام as something bestowed before any human act of return.
terra: The she-camel has an assigned drinking turn shared with the people, making her a protected participant in a measured order rather than sacrificial property.
terra: The explicit command not to touch her with harm supplies the negative boundary to lawful ritual slaughter.
terra: They hamstring her and become regretful, repeating the reversal in which killing the marked animal violates God's command.
terra: Solomon voices رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ; the favor is answered by spoken acknowledgement, close to the section's insistence that this surah's commanded return is speech.
terra: Solomon calls the throne's arrival a favor from his Lord that tests whether he will thank or deny; the given good immediately poses the question of counter-response.
luna: The section's reciprocal reading is that one answers what God has given with an offering to Him. This ayah states the parallel principle directly: do good as Allah has done good to you.
terra: God gives Luqman wisdom with the injunction to thank Him, presenting divine gift and grateful response as a single commission.
terra: God lavishes outward and inward favors, yet some dispute about Him without guidance; favor and the absence of guidance are placed in a revealing opposition.
terra: اعْمَلُوا آلَ دَاوُودَ شُكْرًا makes grateful work a response to divine giving; it complements the section's observation that surah 93 assigns spoken narration as its response.
terra: Saba is told to eat its Lord's provision and give thanks; received sustenance is explicitly converted into grateful response.
terra: Saba turns away after the command to eat and thank in 34:15, and its two gardens are exchanged for inferior growth; failed response changes the gift.
terra: The consequence is explicitly called repayment for ingratitude, a punitive reversal of the section's grateful counter-gift.

luna: The section reads sacrifice as a return for what God has given. This ayah states a specific reciprocal movement: what people spend is replaced by God, the best provider. It presents that giving relation in the opposite direction, without naming sacrifice.
terra: God creates أَنْعَامًا for human beings and gives them possession, so the animal that may be offered is first something received.
terra: The livestock are subjected for riding and eating, specifying the animal's gifted availability that the sacrificial use presupposes.
terra: Benefits and drinks from the livestock end with أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ, making gratitude the demanded return for the animal-gift.
terra: Abraham says إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ just before the granted-son and sacrifice sequence; guidance toward the Lord frames the later offering.
terra: Abraham asks his Lord for a righteous child, establishing the requested gift whose surrender the following scene will test.
terra: God announces a forbearing son in answer to 37:100; this is the received gift that 37:102 places in the sacrificial counter-movement.
terra: Abraham tells his granted son that he sees himself sacrificing him, and the son consents; a received gift is placed back at the giver's disposal in the scene's starkest form.
terra: Their submission and the son's being laid down make the intended sacrifice an enacted scene rather than a general statement about devotion.
terra: The vision is declared fulfilled before the killing occurs and the doer is rewarded, showing that obedient surrender, rather than flesh as such, is accepted.
terra: Calling the event الْبَلَاءُ الْمُبِينُ defines the attempted offering as a test, clarifying why intention and submission can complete it before the animal ransom.
terra: وَفَدَيْنَاهُ بِذِبْحٍ عَظِيمٍ turns the intended human sacrifice into a great sacrificial animal, completing the scene most directly associated with the offering feast.
terra: هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا is followed by permission to bestow or withhold, showing a divine gift placed in a recipient's hands and capable of passing onward.
terra: God makes livestock for riding and eating, again locating the offering animal among benefits deliberately given to people.
terra: Further benefits and fulfilled needs culminate in travel on livestock and ships; the animal is both provision and a means of directed arrival.

luna: The section's source dictionary root ن ع م names camels; this ayah explicitly names الْأَنْعَامِ as animals people ride. It supplies a Qur'anic scene for the animal branch of the section's root note. | terra: God makes ships and الْأَنْعَام as mounts; the livestock sense of the section's ن ع م root is presented as something made available to people.

luna: The section names نعمة as the Lord's blessing and ends by commanding its narration. Here riders are told to remember نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ and praise the One who subjected the mount; 43:12 supplies the livestock being ridden. | terra: On mounting those animals, people are told to remember نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكُمْ; together with 43:12 this explicitly joins the livestock and favor branches of ن ع م and answers favor with speech.

luna: This is a parallel, not the same destination: the section reads the animal's movement toward the Haram as sacred direction, while the rider's travel formula begun in 43:13 ends with إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ, naming the human return to God.
terra: The mature believer voices a prayer to thank God's نِعْمَة and do pleasing good, another spoken conversion of received favor into response.
terra: The peoples' gods taken as قُرْبَانًا fail to help them, showing an offering aimed at nearness but directed to recipients who cannot receive or answer it.
terra: God promises to complete His favor upon the Prophet and guide him on a straight path, directly joining the section's favor and guidance roots around the same addressee.

luna: The section's hedy moves toward its destination; this ayah states that the offering was prevented from reaching its place. That interruption is the direct reversal of the animal's intended arrival. | terra: The hedy is held back أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ; obstructed arrival supplies the exact reversal of the section's animal guided to its sanctuary destination.

luna: The section's hedy is directed toward the Haram; 48:25 says it was blocked from its destination. This ayah completes the interrupted pilgrimage scene by promising the believers entry into the Sacred Mosque in safety. | terra: The truthful vision promises safe entry into the Sacred Mosque, completing in prospect the sanctuary journey whose pilgrims and hedy were blocked in 48:25.

terra: People count their submission as a favor to the Messenger, but God reverses the direction: بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ; guidance itself is the divine favor, not a human payment to Him.
terra: Abraham withdraws to his household and brings a fat calf, contributing the preparation of the animal gift that 51:27 actually presents.
terra: Abraham brings the calf near to his guests and asks why they do not eat, concretely staging an animal presented to intended recipients.
terra: After the calf is not received, the visitors reassure Abraham and announce a learned son; the animal gift is followed by a divine gift in the reverse order from the sacrifice narrative.
terra: The person who gives only a little and then stops reverses the open divine gift and wholehearted responsive giving developed in the section.
terra: God sends the she-camel as a trial and commands watchful patience, so the human response demanded by this animal is restraint.
terra: The water is apportioned between people and camel, specifying the inviolable arrangement tested by the following killing.
terra: They summon their companion and he hamstrings the camel, the act that violates the trial rather than completing an offering.
terra: وَلَا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ forbids giving in order to obtain more, setting a boundary around the section's reciprocal reading: response to a gift is not bargaining for an increase.
terra: Feeding the needy, orphan, and captive despite love of the food parallels the distribution of sacrificial meat, while 76:9 supplies its non-transactional intention.
terra: The feeders say they seek God's face and want neither recompense nor thanks from recipients; this prevents the sacrificial poor-share in 76:8 from becoming a transaction with the poor.
terra: The afterlife recompense is called عَطَاءً from the Lord; here the named given thing is itself a return, a useful counterpart to the section's voluntary counter-gift.

luna: The section's source root for ضحى links the morning to an Eid offering. This ayah says God darkened night and brought out its ضُحَى; it echoes the Surah 93 opening's day-and-night frame around the image's named morning. | terra: وَأَخْرَجَ ضُحَاهَا sets the earth's daylight against its darkened night; this clarifies the base daylight sense underneath the section's secondary sacrificial branch.
terra: Not urging one another to feed the poor supplies another specific failure of the sharing that accompanies the offered animal.

luna: The section's dictionary form الأضحية ties ḍuḥā to the animal slaughtered on Eid. This ayah uses the same root in ضُحَاهَا for the sun's morning brightness, keeping the sacrifice-time word connected to its daylight sense. | terra: The oath وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا repeats the ض ح و family in another oath, preserving the daylight sense from which the section hears the sacrificial-day noun.
terra: The messenger identifies نَاقَةَ اللَّهِ and its drinking right, marking a consecrated camel that must be protected rather than presumed available for sacrifice.
terra: The people's hamstringing of that camel brings destruction; unlawful killing of a divinely marked animal reverses obedient ritual slaughter.

luna: The section's gift root ʿaṭā becomes an offering in its reciprocal reading. This ayah contributes the person who gives and is mindful; 92:7 completes the sequence by promising that God will ease that person's way, reversing the section's order of divine giving followed by human response. | terra: مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَاتَّقَىٰ joins giving to taqwa; it links the section's gift root with the inward quality that determines whether an offering reaches or is accepted.
terra: The God-fearing person gives wealth to purify himself; 92:19-20 then define this return as free of human repayment and directed solely to the Lord.
terra: No one's favor is being repaid by this giver, sharply distinguishing devotion to God from a balanced human exchange account.
terra: The giving seeks only the face of the Most High Lord, fixing the recipient and motive of the offered response.
terra: فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ commands a response directed to the Lord of the sanctuary; 106:4 supplies the gifts that motivate it.
terra: Feeding against hunger and security against fear are the received gifts behind 106:3's worship of the Lord of the House, paralleling gift followed by offered response.
terra: Failure even to urge feeding the poor reverses the sacrificial distribution in which received livestock becomes food for the needy.

luna: The section names the root ع ط و through يُعْطِيكَ in 93:5; 108:1 addresses the same Prophet with أَعْطَيْنَاكَ, making the Lord's gift explicit. The following ayah supplies the sacrificial response. | terra: The same named ع ط و root gives the Prophet a gift from his Lord, إِنَّا أَعْطَيْنَاكَ الْكَوْثَرَ, establishing the received side of the section's gift-and-offering movement.

luna: The section reads sacrifice as a response to what the Lord gives; after the gift in 108:1, this ayah commands فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ. Its own contribution is the prayer and slaughter directed to the Lord. | terra: فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَانْحَرْ makes prayer and sacrifice the immediate response to 108:1's divine gift, the section's closest explicit counterpart.
